title: Lazy-Sunday Korean Beef Flank Steak Sujebi
description: A comforting, lacto-vegetarian-friendly Korean Busan-style dish featuring a flavorful stir-fry and tender beef flank steak, all wrapped up in a delicious sujebi form served in a donabe vessel.
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of canola oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Slice the beef flank steak into thin strips and add to the skillet, cooking for 3-4 minutes or until browned.
Remove the beef from the skillet and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of canola oil and sauté the sliced onion and minced garlic until softened, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the grated ginger and cook for an additional minute.

Add the beef back into the skillet, along with the hot pepper flakes, ground black pepper, Korean chili paste gochujang, fish sauce, and Korean chili flakes gochugaru. Stir-fry until the beef is cooked through, about 4-5 minutes.
Season the beef mixture with salt to taste.
Meanwhile, cook the sujebi dough according to package instructions or recipe.
To assemble the sujebi, place a piece of cooked sujebi dough in the bottom of a donabe vessel, followed by a portion of the beef mixture, and finish with a sprinkle of green onions.
Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used, ending with a layer of sujebi dough on top.
